questions.q: What is the first question in the diagnostic sequence this case study follows for an unreachable instance?
options: Is the instance actually in a running state?
Does the security group allow port 22?
Is there a route to the internet gateway?
Does the instance have a public IP?
questions.explain: Checking instance state comes first — it rules out a crashed or stopped instance before anything else is investigated.

questions.q: What did describe-instances reveal about meridian-web2's PublicIpAddress field?
options: It was null — the instance had no public IP address at all
It showed a valid public IP that simply wasn't responding
It showed two public IP addresses, which caused a conflict
The field was not returned by the API
questions.explain: A null PublicIpAddress immediately tells you SSH from outside the VPC can never reach the instance, regardless of security group rules.

questions.q: What was the actual root cause of meridian-web2 being unreachable?
options: It was launched into the private subnet instead of the public subnet, by a copy-pasted subnet ID
Its security group blocked all inbound traffic
The internet gateway itself was detached from the VPC
The instance's AMI did not include an SSH server
questions.explain: SubnetId showed meridian-web2 in subnet-0meridianpriv, the app tier's private subnet from Lesson 29 — the wrong subnet entirely.

questions.q: Why was it still worth running describe-route-tables even after the subnet mistake was already suspected?
options: To confirm the route table wasn't also a contributing factor, rather than assuming based on one clue
Because route tables are checked first in every troubleshooting scenario
Because AWS requires a route-table check before terminating an instance
It wasn't worth running and added no value
questions.explain: Confirming each layer rather than guessing is the point of a diagnostic sequence — it came back clean, which ruled that layer out for certain.

questions.q: Why did the fix require terminating meridian-web2 rather than just moving it to the public subnet?
options: An EC2 instance's subnet cannot be changed after it has been launched
AWS charges extra to change an instance's subnet without terminating it
Terminating is always required before any security group change
The private subnet itself had to be deleted first
questions.explain: Subnet assignment is fixed at launch, so correcting it means terminating the misplaced instance and relaunching in the right subnet.
